fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Look at what verse 3 does: “Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man…” The offerings are right there, and the LORD still sets them beside awful things. Then He says what is going on: “Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.” (Isaiah 66:3). So the problem isn't that they brought something. It's that they did it their own way and not His.

That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “…because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.” (Isaiah 66:4). His reason isn't a missed rule. It's that He spoke and nobody paid Him any mind. I think this part is heavy. Then the verse says what they did instead: “But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”

problems.problem: It points out the contrast but does not explain beyond saying the offering is not the whole story; the explanation still feels flat.
It repeats and quotes the verse without meaningfully explaining the reason the LORD gives.
